minor.issue: The asyncio.wait_for timeout (20 s / 60 s) also counts the time spent waiting for the global ai_advisor._gate semaphore and the 2/5/10 s 429 retries. With 3 bots sharing the Emergent key (1 request at a time), a stage-1 call waiting behind another bot's stage-2 Sonnet evaluation (10–30 s) can time out → signal stored as ERROR (fail-safe reject) even though the provider is fine. ai_ms likewise includes queue time. Suggest applying the timeout only around the actual stream (inside _serialized), or giving stage 1 a timeout that does not include the queue.

Not validated against the active provider or source. If the override is claude-* and the user switches to Gemini or OpenAI, every stage-1 call fails → all short-horizon signals become ERROR. Suggest validating against FAST_MODEL_OPTIONS[provider] or resetting the override to '' when the provider/source changes.

mean_reversion sets tp = bb_mid (strategies.py ~L68), so its R:R is often < 1.5. With the default min_rr 1.5 most mean_reversion short-horizon signals will now be blocked as RR_BAJO. Confirm this is intended or exempt strategies whose TP is not ATR-based.

Confirm the RR_BAJO impact on mean_reversion (TP at the BB middle band)
critical_code_review_comments: FX _handle_signal passes settings.timeframe (not tf) to quick_filter/final_eval. This matches the existing behaviour, but slow/long signals with their own tf would show the wrong TF (only matters if long horizon ever reaches the funnel; today stage 1 is short-only).
Stage 1 sets chat._probe=False, so a failure of the cheap model marks the main AI health as failing (AiHealthBanner) even when the main model is fine. Probably acceptable, but worth knowing.
Settings PUTs from tests generate change/restore events in changes/fx_changes/pep_changes (see testing_notes). They were not deleted here.
